pred_ddx.label: Fetal Brain Anomaly (e.g. Agenesis of Corpus Callosum or Dandy-Walker Malformation)

Congenital Infection (e.g. CMV): The presence of bilateral ventriculomegaly, irregular ventricular walls, and multiple hyperechoic regions within the ventricles on ultrasound, along with high signal intensity on T1-weighted and low signal intensity on T2-weighted MRI images, are suggestive of an intrauterine infection. Although the TORCH panel was normal, it does not entirely rule out congenital infection, particularly CMV, which can have a variable presentation and may not always be detected by standard tests.
